content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Identify the main air pollutants and their sources
Explain the problems caused by each pollutant
Describe how catalytic converters reduce pollution
Discuss methods to reduce air pollution

refers to harmful substances released into the atmosphere that can damage health, ecosystems, and buildings. Most air pollution comes from burning fossil fuels, but industrial processes and agriculture also contribute.
Occurs when oxygen supply is limited

$$2\text{C} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{CO}$$ (limited oxygen)  Compare with complete combustion: $$\text{C} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2$$ (excess oxygen)  **Problems:** | Problem | Explanation | |---------|-------------| | Toxic to humans | Binds to haemoglobin in blood | | Reduces oxygen transport | Haemoglobin can't carry oxygen | | Colourless and odourless | Hard to detect | | Can cause death | In enclosed spaces |  **Reducing CO emissions:** - Ensure complete combustion (sufficient oxygen) - Regular vehicle maintenance - Catalytic converters in vehicles  ### Nitrogen Oxides (NOₓ)  **Sources:** - High temperature combustion (car engines, power stations) - Nitrogen and oxygen from air react at high temperatures  **Formation:** $$\text{N}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{NO}$$

Explain how carbon monoxide is formed and why it is dangerous.
Carbon monoxide is formed by incomplete combustion
Occurs when carbon-containing fuels burn with insufficient oxygen
Common in car engines, faulty boilers, blocked chimneys
Carbon monoxide binds to haemoglobin in red blood cells
It binds more strongly than oxygen
Haemoglobin cannot carry oxygen to body tissues
Can be fatal in high concentrations
Colourless and odourless, so hard to detect
Describe how a catalytic converter reduces air pollution from vehicle exhausts.
Catalytic converters are fitted to vehicle exhausts
They contain precious metal catalysts (platinum, palladium, rhodium)
These catalysts speed up reactions that convert harmful gases
Carbon monoxide is oxidised to carbon dioxide:
Nitrogen oxides are reduced to nitrogen:
Harmful CO, hydrocarbons, and NOₓ are converted
Products are less harmful (CO₂, H₂O, N₂)
Explain how power stations can reduce sulfur dioxide emissions.
Coal and oil contain sulfur impurities
When burned, sulfur dioxide (SO₂) is produced
SO₂ causes acid rain and respiratory problems
Exhaust gases pass through a scrubber
Calcium oxide or calcium hydroxide is used
Can be oxidised to calcium sulfate (gypsum)
Gypsum can be sold for building materials
Widely used in modern power stations
They convert CO to CO₂ (which is less immediately harmful)
Thinking electric vehicles produce no pollution
They produce no direct emissions, but electricity generation may cause pollution
